tara: I pushed a short note outlining an adaptive-batcher admission handshake. Goal: make admission deterministic across hosts while allowing soft-borrowing for bursty tenants. Posting here for quick feedback.

gil: nice. can you show the handshake steps briefly? we had nondeterministic admits last week causing reorders.

tara: Sure — sketch: 
```
1) request -> route-eval (qos, max_delay_ms, cache_mode)
2) pre-admit: probe local headroom + kv-cache probe
3) tentative-reserve -> returns admit_token (lease_ms)
4) enqueue with admit_token -> at dispatch, token validated else fallback
5) token expiry => either re-reserve or fallback to cheaper model-variant
```

nate: admit_token is good. how do we avoid token-grab races across replicas? thought: token carries node_id + nonce and sequenced by leader for that tenant shard. If leader is unavailable, allow best-effort local accept with `reconcile_on_commit`.

yana: telemetry: emit `admission.token_issued`, `admission.token_validated`, `admission.token_expired`, and `admission.fallback_reason`. Also track `borrow_usage_pct` per tenant. That will help tune borrow_limit.

tara: borrowing semantics: each tenant has reserved_capacity and dynamic_borrow up to borrow_limit_pct of cluster_free. Borrow score increments when borrowing and decays with half-life T (configurable). On high borrow_score, tenant deprioritized for further borrow until decay.

gil: fallback policy note: prefer cheaper quantized variant only if `route.qos.allow_cost_fallback=true` and request not marked `latency_critical`. Add explicit fields in route-config.

ops-bot: monitor: node-17 queue-depth spike at 1748054370, auto-evict applied to tenant=test-bench, reason=manual-evict

tara: OK action items: (1) I'll draft an RFC with admit_token proto & leader reconciliation sketch. (2) @nate will prototype token leader for a tenant-shard. (3) @yana will add the telemetry counters to staging. Meet in 48h to sync on simulator results.

yana: I'll also add histogram for `token_lifetime_ms` and `revalidation_latency_ms`.

tara: thanks, team — I'll open the RFC and add the canary rollout: 3% traffic, monitor p50/p90/p99, borrow_usage, token_expiry rate.
